subject: Purchase lanes, co-sell credit mechanics, and billing implications for pilot
messages:
From: Julia Nguyen <julia.nguyen@medilink.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medilink.com
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q on AWS listing vs direct contract for the pilot

Hi Kimberly,

We're getting internal pushback from procurement on whether we should buy the 3-month pilot through AWS Marketplace (private offer or standard listing) or via a direct Redwood invoice / PO. The main asks are:
- Which route results in the fastest PO-to-invoice timeline?
- Does choosing Marketplace vs Direct affect eligibility for co-sell credits / rebate tracking with our AWS rep?
- Any material differences in taxes, fees, or support entitlements we should expect?

Procurement also asked if a private offer works the same as a direct invoice from Redwood in terms of purchase order wording. Attached is our questionnaire — can you take a look?

Thanks,
Julia Nguyen
Head of Platform Ops
MediLink Health

Attachment: Procurement_Questionnaire_MediLink.xlsx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on AWS listing vs direct contract for the pilot

Hi Julia — thanks for the questionnaire, that helps. Short answer up front: both lanes can work, but they have different procurement mechanics and timing trade-offs. Below is a summarized comparison and concrete next steps.

High-level differences:
- AWS Marketplace (Public listing vs Private Offer): Private Offer is the usual way to preserve the marketplace procurement path while allowing negotiated pricing. The PO is accepted by AWS and then routed to Redwood — that typically shortens legal review because procurement only needs to accept the private offer rather than negotiate an MSA. Marketplace invoices go through AWS (AWS bills MediLink and remits to Redwood).
- Direct invoice / Redwood SOW: Redwood issues an invoice/PO directly to you under our MSA. This is cleaner for customers who need consolidated billing to a single vendor or have specific tax/PO requirements. It can take longer if procurement requires MSA redlines.

Co-sell / rebate implications:
- Co-sell credit: If you buy via a Marketplace Private Offer and your AWS rep registers the opportunity, that purchase is eligible for partner co-sell credit on Redwood side (subject to AWS registration rules). Direct invoices can also be credited for co-sell but typically require explicit partner registration and invoice mapping on our side. Vanessa (copied) can confirm the best path to maximize co-sell credit.

Taxes and fees:
- Marketplace invoices: AWS handles tax calculation and remittance for the invoice it issues. That can simplify tax handling for MediLink but you see AWS line items (including a marketplace fee).
- Direct invoices: Redwood handles invoicing and tax. We can provide tax forms, but procurement teams sometimes prefer the marketplace tax flow for simplicity.

Support / entitlements:
- Functionally the pilot support is identical regardless of billing lane. Who you deal with for billing disputes differs (AWS vs Redwood).

Proposal / next steps:
1) If speed-to-PO is the priority: go Private Offer via AWS Marketplace. I attached a draft Private Offer we can publish and send to your procurement for acceptance.
2) If consolidated vendor invoicing / custom tax handling is required: we do a short SOW + direct invoice.

I attached a sample Private Offer draft and a short sample PO language below. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk procurement through both lanes.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Private_Offer_Draft.pdf

---
Sample PO wording (copyable):

PO to: Redwood Inference, Inc.
Reference: Redwood SOW #RL-2027-03-01 or AWS Marketplace Private Offer ID [to be filled]
Total: USD [amount]
Payment terms: Net 30

(Notes: For Private Offer purchases processed through AWS, please include the AWS Private Offer ID on the PO. For direct invoices, reference the Redwood SOW number.)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q on AWS listing vs direct contract for the pilot

Adding a few channel notes from partner/co-sell side.

- Co-sell recognition: Private Offer + registered opportunity is the cleanest route for automatic co-sell attribution. If you prefer a direct invoice, we can still attach the sale to the AWS registration but it requires an extra reconciliation step on our end.
- Pricing parity: Private Offers can include negotiated discounts off catalog price; make clear whether the discount should be applied to the catalog SKU or via credit line in the Private Offer.
- Timeline expectations: Private Offer acceptance by procurement -> AWS processes within 3–5 business days typically. Direct invoice route depends on your procurement MSA cadence (sometimes 2–4 weeks).

Internal link: Co-sell playbook (internal) — https://partner.redwood/internal/co-sell-playbook (for our ops folks).

If MediLink needs to attribute partner incentive to an internal AWS rep, flag the rep name in the private offer comments so accounting can map it.

—Vanessa
Head of GTM Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Julia — answers inline and attaching a plain-text sample PO for easy copy/paste.

1) Sample PO language (attached as Sample_PO_Language.txt) — minimal fields your system likes:
- Vendor: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Vendor Tax ID: 12-3456789
- Description: 3-month pilot — Redwood Gen-2 inference (Pilot SKU RL-PILOT-3M)
- Reference: AWS Private Offer ID [if applicable] or Redwood SOW RL-2027-03-01
- Unit price, qty, total, payment terms Net 30

2) Pricing parity and marketplace fees:
- Private Offer: the price you accept in the Private Offer is the price AWS will present on your invoice. AWS will show its marketplace fee as a separate line item; the net to Redwood reflects the negotiated amount after AWS fees. In practice, we set the Private Offer to reflect the negotiated price so the total you pay matches expectations; the line items may still show AWS fee components.
- Direct invoice: Redwood invoice equals the negotiated price; no marketplace fee line item.

3) Tax handling:
- Private Offer / Marketplace invoice: AWS calculates and remits taxes on the invoice it issues.
- Direct invoice: Redwood calculates and remits taxes on our invoice. If you need specific tax forms, Redwood can provide them for direct invoice purchases.

Next steps:
- I uploaded the Private Offer draft (attached) — if Medilink procurement is comfortable with the PO wording, we can publish the offer and send it to you for acceptance. That will probably get you to invoice fastest.
- If you need consolidated vendor billing or special T&Cs, let's switch to direct SOW.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call tomorrow morning to finalize.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
